facts.topic: present empty fade, defaults and color retention
facts.contract: A present Fade is dispatched even if its time and color optionals are absent. The native fade consumer uses time defaults(1,.5,1). When the animation has no keyframes, present RGB is copied as float RGB with alpha1, otherwise color defaults to black with alpha1. If keyframes already exist, color assignment is skipped, retaining the existing fade color. There is no divide-by255 conversion in this consumer.

facts.topic: fade phase limits and minimum total
facts.contract: The packet preprocessor clamps each present fade time to[0,10]. The animation helper rejects negative phase lengths or opacity and extends wait to max(wait,.5-in-out). It then merges three points(in,1),(in+wait,1),(in+wait+out,0). A new empty curve has an implicit starting point(0,0) for interpolation, rather than an additional stored zero keyframe. This distinction matters at the helper epsilon boundary.

facts.topic: overlapping fade timeline and keyframe selection
facts.contract: Before merging a new fade, subtract current elapsed time from existing key times and discard negative-time keys. If keys remain, insert(0,currentValue); reset elapsed to0. For each requested new point, evaluate the old piecewise-linear curve. With epsilon=float.0001, skip insertion if oldValue+epsilon>=newValue and lastTime+epsilon>=newTime. Otherwise insert in time order, or replace the value of a preceding key whose time is within epsilon of newTime. Then remove any middle key whose two neighbor values are both at least its value. This is the recovered insertion/pruning rule; it is not an assertion that the algorithm computes the exact mathematical pointwise maximum of two continuous curves.

facts.topic: spring easing function and pose/FOV selection
facts.contract: For finite progress, Spring clamps u to[0,1], samples the sine lookup at truncateToInt32(((2.5*u*u*u+.2)*(pi*u))*10430.3779296875) modulo65536, and forms ((sample*powf(1-u,2.2)+u)*(1+1.2*(1-u))). It returns start+(end-start)*that value. This is neither an exponential damping formula nor a direct arbitrary-frequency cosine. The same lookup table of easing function pointers selects this function for pose CameraBlendStateComponent and custom FOV easing. Float operation order and the imported CRT functions remain numerical details.

facts.topic: spring sine table construction and reuse boundary
facts.contract: The native sine table is uninitialized .data on disk. Its initializer fills65536 temporary floats by calling imported CRT sinf(float(i)/10430.3779296875f), then copies them to the global table. This uses division, unlike Perlin’s separate legacy algorithmic SineTable multiplication path. The existing CurrentSineEntry data uses the corresponding division-style convention, but exact equality to this client’s runtime CRT output has not been proven. Comparing the existing data to a double-precision sin of the binary32 angle, rounded to binary32, differs at86 entries by1ULP; this is not a captured native table hash.

facts.topic: typed instruction enqueue order does not prove final precedence
facts.contract: The preprocessor handles fields in order Set, Target, RemoveTarget, Clear, Fade, FOV, Spline, Attach, Detach. These are separate typed event queues/listeners. Most listeners append a one-field CameraInstruction to the global instruction vector; Fade updates its own global component. The complete event-queue drain schedule has not been established, so this list must not be presented as verified final precedence for a deliberately combined multi-action packet.

facts.topic: shake action dispatch and stop scope
facts.contract: CameraShake action0 adds a shake, action1 stops, and any other action returns. Add requires a local player and enabled user option0x23A, then forwards type, intensity and duration to CameraShakeComponent::queueShakeEvent. Stop removes the local player’s entire CameraShakeComponent and does not read the packet shake type. Thus this handler supports Stop-all, not a type-specific stop conclusion. Noise generation, overlap blending and option naming were not closed.

limits: Runtime findings are matched protocol2193 evidence; protocol2225 equivalence has not been established.
No Minecraft executable, DLL or machine-code fragment was run. No captured native trajectory, frame output or sine-table memory is claimed.
The table comparison does not establish exact CRT sinf or powf bit behavior on the user’s Windows system.
Final multi-field instruction precedence requires event-queue scheduling evidence beyond enqueue order.
Complete preset inheritance/default construction, malformed numeric handling and the vanilla ease allowlist are not closed here.
Focus target snap, continue-targeting, yaw-limit/angle conventions, aim-assist and custom-camera rendering interactions are not fully reverse-engineered.
Attach pool filtering is established; full final boom position/locator fallback and exact detach behavior are not.
Spline findings are delegated to camera_spline_reference/findings metadata; no spline completion rule is asserted by this artifact.
Shake action routing/Stop-all are established; native noise distribution, overlap and complete option behavior remain unresolved.
